body.statement:
For the nested construction/calibration/evaluation estimator, under the construction-sample bridge rates, multiplier and calibration envelopes, Gram cutoff, affine coefficient envelope, and corrected projection balance, the exact cell expansion implies
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)}-D^0_{J_n}\|_{L^2(P;\ell^2)}=O_p(\delta_{D,n}),
 \qquad
 \delta_{D,n}=\left(\sum_{c=1}^{J_n}d_{c,n}^2\right)^{1/2}
 \le\sqrt{J_n}\max_{c\le J_n}d_{c,n}.
\]
The independent calibration sample satisfies the rates in \(\mathrm{lem:conditional-calibration-concentration}\).  If \(\Pi_{R,J_n}\) projects onto the positive population Gram eigenspace, then
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat\Pi_k^C-\Pi_{R,J_n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(\eta_{\Pi,n}),
\]
and
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat b^{(-k,C\mid A)\top}\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k,A)}
 -b_{J_n}^\top D^0_{J_n}\|_2
 =O_p\!\left[L_n\delta_{D,n}
 +\frac{\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}}{\kappa_{J_n}}
 \left\{\zeta_{c,n}+(\zeta_{G,n}+\rho_n)L_n
 +\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}B_{0,n}\eta_{\Pi,n}\right\}\right].
\]
Consequently, whenever the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\) hold, the explicit coefficient-to-affine-weight identity gives
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat\psi^{(-k,C\mid A)}-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2
 =O_p(\Gamma_n)=o_p(1).
\]
body.justification: Ridge uniqueness and the deterministic four-corner affine conversion are valid and the exact perturbation equations identify the required controls.
body.gap: The stated primitive list omits multiplier envelopes, dimension-correct aggregation, same-training-sample concentration, and learned-coefficient factors in Gram-null-space perturbations.
body.consumer: Those controls must be added and verified before the affine ensemble is an implementable efficiency-attaining procedure.
body.proof_tex:
For one learned cell write \(\Delta h=\widehat h-h^0\) and \(\Delta q=\widehat q-q^0\).  Direct expansion of the definition of \(S_a\) gives the exact equality
\[
 S_a(\widehat h,\widehat q)-S_a(h^0,q^0)
 =(1-I_aq^0)\Delta h+I_a(Y-h^0)\Delta q-I_a\Delta q\Delta h.
\]
Hölder's inequality, the construction-sample fourth-norm rates, and \(\mathrm{ass:moment-envelope-growth}\) therefore give
\[
 \|S_a(\widehat h,\widehat q)-S_a(h^0,q^0)\|_2
 \le M_{q,n}\|\Delta h\|_4+M_{y,n}\|\Delta q\|_4
 +\|\Delta h\|_4\|\Delta q\|_4
 =O_p(d^S_{a,j\ell,n}).
\]
Every dictionary coordinate is a signed sum of at most four cell signals.  The triangle inequality bounds its \(L^2(P)\) error by the corresponding \(d_{c,n}\).  Summing the squared coordinate bounds proves
\[
 \|\widehat D-D^0\|_{L^2(P;\ell^2)}^2
 =\sum_{c=1}^{J_n}\|\widehat D_c-D_c^0\|_2^2
 =O_p\!\left(\sum_{c=1}^{J_n}d_{c,n}^2\right),
\]
including the stated \(\sqrt{J_n}\) upper bound.  The same calculation for the two base cells gives \(\|\widehat B-B^0\|_2=O_p(d_{0,n})\), where \(B^0=\theta(P)+\phi_0\).

The calibration conclusions follow from \(\mathrm{lem:conditional-calibration-concentration}\), not from evaluation-fold independence.  Let \(G=E[D^0D^{0\top}]\), \(c=E[D^0B^0]\), and let \(\widetilde G=E[\widehat D\widehat D^\top\mid\mathcal D_{A,k}]\) and \(\widetilde c=E[\widehat D\widehat B\mid\mathcal D_{A,k}]\).  Cauchy--Schwarz for Hilbert-space-valued random variables gives
\[
 \|\widetilde G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le \|\widehat D-D^0\|_{L^2(\ell^2)}
 \{\|\widehat D\|_{L^2(\ell^2)}+\|D^0\|_{L^2(\ell^2)}\}
 \le 2\sqrt{J_n}B_{D,n}\delta_{D,n}+\delta_{D,n}^2
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde c-c\|_2
 \le B_{0,n}\delta_{D,n}+(\sqrt{J_n}B_{D,n}+\delta_{D,n})d_{0,n}.
\]
Combining these inequalities with calibration concentration yields
\[
 \|\widehat G_k^C-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(\zeta_{G,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat c_k^C-c\|_2=O_p(\zeta_{c,n}).
\]

All nonzero eigenvalues of \(G\) are at least \(\kappa_{J_n}\).  Since \(\zeta_{G,n}=o_p(\tau_n)\) and \(\tau_n<\kappa_{J_n}/2\), Weyl's variational inequality, obtained directly from \(|u^\top(\widehat G-G)u|\le\|\widehat G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), shows with probability tending to one that eigenvalues arising from \(\ker G\) lie below \(\tau_n\), whereas eigenvalues arising from its range exceed \(\kappa_{J_n}/2\).  Threshold \(\widehat G\) by replacing its eigenvalues at most \(\tau_n\) by zero.  The thresholded operator differs from \(G\) by \(O_p(\zeta_{G,n})\), and both reduced minimum moduli are at least \(\kappa_{J_n}/2\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:operator-kernel-perturbation}\) to these two finite-dimensional operators yields
\[
 \|\widehat\Pi_k^C-\Pi_{R,J_n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =O_p(\zeta_{G,n}/\kappa_{J_n})=O_p(\eta_{\Pi,n}).
\]

By definition, \(Gb_{J_n}=c\), \(b_{J_n}\in\operatorname{range}(G)\), and the cutoff equation is
\[
 (\widehat G_k^C+\rho_n I)\widehat b
 =\widehat\Pi_k^C\widehat c_k^C,
 \qquad \widehat b=\widehat\Pi_k^C\widehat b.
\]
Writing \(\Pi_R=\Pi_{R,J_n}\), using \(G(I-\Pi_R)=0\), and subtracting \(Gb_{J_n}=c\) gives the exact positive-eigenspace equation
\[
 G\Pi_R(\widehat b-b_{J_n})
 =\Pi_R\{(G-\widehat G_k^C)\widehat b
 +(\widehat c_k^C-c)-\rho_n\widehat b
 -(I-\widehat\Pi_k^C)\widehat c_k^C\}.
\]
Because \(c\in\operatorname{range}(G)\),
\[
 \|(I-\widehat\Pi_k^C)\widehat c_k^C\|_2
 \le \zeta_{c,n}+\eta_{\Pi,n}\|c\|_2,
 \qquad
 \|c\|_2\le\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}\,\|B^0\|_2
 \le\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}B_{0,n}.
\]
Inversion of \(G\) on its positive eigenspace and the coefficient envelope now give
\[
 \|\Pi_R(\widehat b-b_{J_n})\|_2
 \le \frac{C}{\kappa_{J_n}}
 \{\zeta_{c,n}+(\zeta_{G,n}+\rho_n)L_n
 +\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}B_{0,n}\eta_{\Pi,n}\}.
\]
Since \(\|v^\top D^0\|_2=\|G^{1/2}v\|_2\le\sqrt{\Lambda_{J_n}}\|\Pi_Rv\|_2\), while \(\|\widehat b^\top(\widehat D-D^0)\|_2\le L_n\delta_{D,n}\), the asserted prediction bound follows.  This calculation explicitly retains both the Gram-perturbation and ridge terms multiplied by \(L_n\).

It remains to verify the affine conversion.  Collecting the coefficient of every cell in the displayed weight map gives
\[
 \sum_{j,\ell}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_at_a\sum_{j,\ell}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}\widehat S_{a,j\ell}
 =\widehat B-\widehat b^\top\widehat D.
\]
The same identity holds at the population coefficient.  By \(\mathrm{lem:normal-affine-identity}\), every coordinate of \(D^0\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_P\) and has mean zero.  Hence, for every \(b\), orthogonality gives
\[
 \|\phi_0-b^\top D^0\|_2^2
 =\|\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0\|_2^2
 +\|\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0-b^\top D^0\|_2^2.
\]
Thus the coefficient \(b_{J_n}\), defined by minimizing the left side on the positive Gram eigenspace, also minimizes the second term and attains \(\alpha_{J_n}\).  Under \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\),
\[
 \|B^0-b_{J_n}^\top D^0-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2
 =\|\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0-b_{J_n}^\top D^0\|_2
 \le\alpha_{J_n}.
\]
Adding the base-cell error, learned-dictionary prediction error, and sieve approximation gives \(O_p(\Gamma_n)=o_p(1)\), as claimed.
